question.text: Ms. Sneha Iyer is IR head at Zephyr Mid-Market AIF. A Canadian pension fund's DD team arrives for a 3-day on-site. On Day 1 the lead ODD specialist asks to meet the fund accountant and investment team, review 2 months of bank reconciliations, and review the most recent Investment Committee minutes and a sample IC paper. Her BEST response is:

answer.text: Decline operational interviews — accompany all meetings to ensure consistent messaging.
Decline the IC document review — IC papers and minutes are confidential under the IMA.

Accommodate all three requests — on-site meetings with the investment manager and relevant teams, document review with physical verification of staff/policies/procedures, and review of IC minutes plus sample IC material are source-backed institutional ODD practices.
Accommodate only the document review; refuse all meetings citing operational protocols.

explanation.text: The Logic: Per Chapter 12, institutional due diligence emphasises on-site visits to physically verify the existence of staff members, policies and procedures, meetings with the investment manager and relevant teams, and review of Investment Committee minutes and sample IC papers. A transparent, fully co-operative response signals strong controls. The Trap: Options A, B and D all restrict source-backed DD access — precisely what institutional LPs interpret as weak controls or governance hesitation. Note: The workbook explicitly lists on-site visits, document verification, manager/team meetings, and IC document review as standard elements of investor-side operational due diligence.
